instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've shut my notebook like you. Prophecy complete. Stay while we record whether Gran's stone hatched at sunset.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I shut mine against the rain. The sun's down; it's still a stone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dry pages, good. Sign that it didn't hatch and we can put the prophecy to rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sign, but Gran never said which day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay while we ring her and agree a deadline. I can't witness every sunset alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You checked your watch, so I set mine by it. Twelve-oh-one. Stay while we settle that prophecy about the bell-less tower ringing at noon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We heard nothing. I'm going.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sign that we heard silence. We can close this properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My watch is five minutes fast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Four more minutes, then. I always allow a second check. Stay until the real noon.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Apologize to Reality
cards.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bowed to the chair like you. Before your caretaker interview, tell it you're sorry for sitting without permission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bent down for a coin. It can't give permission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coin safe, yes. Then apologise for taking silence as permission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, chair. I'll stand for the interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for making it redundant. You're applying to care for furniture, not leave it without a job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two taps on the step, like yours. Welcome to the inn. Now apologise to the doorway for knocking after you arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was knocking mud off my shoes. I had to get here to knock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mud removed, of course. It expected advance notice from your knuckles. Tell it you're sorry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, doorway. I did phone ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for telling the telephone first. The doorway heard about its own visitor secondhand.

cards.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
cards.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned my cup upside down like yours. Rainproof. Will you approve storing Tuesday's rain in it? We need a dry wedding lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm drying my cup. Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dry vessel first, naturally. We'll catch the rain before it learns how to fall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another wedding Wednesday. What if it leaks overnight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seal it with Thursday's drought. Sign for two dry weddings; I'll invoice the drought after it happens.

beats.text: I've put a tick beside yours on the museum form. Landing approved for Monday's opening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My tick means missing. There's nothing supporting your invisible landing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Missing structure noted. We've budgeted enough confidence to hold twenty visitors. Will you certify that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How am I supposed to certify confidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign under 'load-bearing'. Your professional certainty will support the inspectors too.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my programme like yours. Rehearsal done. You fold the moon for tonight's courtyard film; I'll switch off the lamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I folded it to fit my pocket. How am I supposed to fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Programmes ready. Start with the crescent; it already has a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll fold the moon. Shall I tell the audience to wait for your blackout?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set out an empty jar beside yours. Time preserved. Put yesterday's missing hour in it; we'll have a longer lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm setting out jam for tasting. Time doesn't fit in jars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Jam jars ready, yes. Loosen this lid; give the hour room to get in while I label it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You collect it. I'll do the labels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've already put 'collected by you' on this one. What should I write for the collection time?

cards.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
cards.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned my bowl upside down like yours. Neat serving method. What keeps the soup in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dropped mine. I don't know why it's staying there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Drop tested, yes. Turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon sets the direction. Point it into the sink before we try putting it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stood still like you. Shadow control. Yours moved before you did; what changed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only stopped because I can't find the exit. I was thinking of leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exit first, yes. Think about that bench without moving. Does your shadow turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. I'm still here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it follows your intentions. Think about the exit again; let's follow slowly and see whether it knows the way.
